the without Mn alloy comprises a-Mg, Mg24Y5, and Al2Y phases
The network morphology corresponds to the Mg24Y5 phase
both the particulate and acicular forms are attributed to the Al2Y phase
The lamellar phase is identified as LPSO/SFs (Ref 10). The absence of the characteristic diffraction peak for the LPSO/SFs phase in the XRD pattern (Fig. 2) is due to its scarcity.
The alloy adding Mn is still composed of the above phases, and no new diffraction peak is observed.
The network phase (Mark 1) is predominantly constituted by Mg and Y, which, combined with XRD data, is identified as the Mg24Y5 phase

attributes.morphology: particulate and acicular; FCC, lattice constant ~0.772 nm
attributes.composition: primarily Al, Y, and Mn with an approximate atomic ratio of 2:1 for Al, Mn and Y

evidence.quote: The particulate phase (Mark 2) and the acicular phase (Mark 3) are primarily composed of Al, Y, and Mn, with an approximate atomic ratio of 2 : 1 for Al, Mn and Y, as shown in Fig. 4(d) and (e), confirming these phases as Al2Y with a minor dissolution of Mn.
Additionally, the lamellar phase (Mark 4) is composed of Mg, Al, and Y, and is identified as the LPSO/SFs phase (Fig. 4f).
the alloy without Mn exhibits the smallest grains (73.2 ± 2.9 lm), characterized by equiaxed dendritic structures
At a Mn concentration of 0.9 wt.%, the alloy's grain morphology shifts to coarse equiaxed dendrites, with the average grain size increasing to 140.5 ± 7.5 lm

conditions.test_method: MTS E44.304 electronic universal testing apparatus; tensile rate 1 mm/min; ambient temperature

evidence.quote: At ambient temperature, the without Mn alloy exhibits superior mechanical properties, with ultimate tensile strength (UTS), yield strength (YS), and elongation (EL) recorded at 216.9 ± 4.2 MPa, 150.2 ± 3.4 MPa, and 6.9 ± 0.3%, respectively.

The abundance of grain boundaries serves as an effective barrier to dislocation movement, ultimately enhancing the alloy's strength (Ref 17, 18).

the Mn atom, with an atomic radius of 0.124 nm that is smaller than the Mg atom's radius of 0.16 nm, can curtail the rate of solute diffusion, thereby reinforcing the Mg matrix and augmenting the alloy's strength and ductility at high temperatures
Introducing Mn into the alloy leads to grain coarsening, thereby efficiently hindering grain boundary migration (Ref 25).

mechanisms.name: dislocation climb hindrance by solute atoms

evidence.quote: solute elements that dissolve within the a-Mg matrix impede dislocation climb during creep (Ref 26).
The considerable difference in atomic radius between Mg and Mn can effectively curtail the solute's diffusion rate, consequently diminishing dislocation movement.

conflicts.description: Abstract and conclusion state the 0.6 wt.% Mn alloy achieves UTS 165.7 ± 3.5 MPa, YS 111.8 ± 2.2 MPa and EL 39.2 ± 2.1% at 300 C, while the microstructure text states 'Mg-8.44Y-0.9Al-xMn ... x = 0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9 wt.%' but Table 1 measured Mn for the 0.6Mn alloy is 0.54 wt.% and for the 0.9Mn alloy is 0.82 wt.%; nominal and measured Mn contents differ.
